narrative_purpose: Shows the forest as a connected food web rather than isolated pairs, so the reader can see how pressure from an apex predator at the top reaches down through links to animals it never touches.
subject: A vertical food-web diagram of glowing animal silhouettes connected by faint luminous threads. At the very top, a single large winged predator with a broad wingspan. Threads run down from it to a middle row of two smaller winged creatures. Threads from those run down to a central cluster of small six-legged herbivore silhouettes. To one side, a separate vertical column on the ground: a mid-sized sleek four-legged-looking pack predator above the herbivore cluster, and at the very bottom a single massive solitary six-limbed predator as the ground-level base. All silhouettes simple and clearly distinct in size and shape, linked by thin glowing lines.
scene: An abstract dark diagrammatic space, faint haze, the silhouettes and threads self-luminous like a constellation map.
camera: Flat head-on diagrammatic view of the vertical web.
light: Self-luminous silhouettes and connecting threads against dark; no external light.
palette: Void-indigo ground, cyan and living-teal silhouettes, a single scarce warm magenta glint on the top apex flyer to draw the eye, threads pale stone-grey.
style: Painterly plate that reads as a wiring diagram through composition alone, soft glowing forms, not a hard vector chart.
detail_level: Moderate: silhouettes simple and clearly different in scale, the top-to-bottom link structure obvious.
composition: Vertical hierarchy filling the frame, apex at top, base at bottom, dark margins on the sides for callouts.
consistency_notes: Creature silhouettes echo the chapter's earlier figures (apex flyer, pack predator, massive ground predator, six-legged grazers). Reads as a teaching diagram.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no tick marks, no arrows, no grid, no diagram chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look
